Definition: Whether national data protection or privacy legislation exists and explicitly covers payment transaction data, including provisions on data collection, storage, sharing, retention, and user rights over their payment data.
Comments: Uganda has general data protection legislation: the Data Protection and Privacy Act (includes privacy protection for customer information) complemented by payment-sector confidentiality/privacy provisions in the National Payment Systems Act (e.g., protection of customer information).

Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Uganda has BoU-operated national payment infrastructure (RTGS and ACH) and widespread nationwide mobile money rails, but a dedicated inclusive instant retail payment scheme (e.g., National Payment Switch) is still described as “in progress,” while BoU’s payment modernization includes adding a 3rd ACH session (Feb 2025) and an RTGS replacement/ISO 20022 migration planned to go live Nov 2025, indicating partially deployed/modernizing rather than a fully deployed nationwide instant payment scheme.

Definition: Whether independent external audits of payment system security, operations, financial controls, and compliance are conducted by third-party auditors, and whether audit results or summaries are made public.
Comments: Independent audits exist publicly for major payment ecosystem participants: MTN Uganda (a key mobile money provider) publishes financial statements (though the referenced interim results are unaudited), and broader group financial statements are audited by external auditors (EY) at MTN Group level, indicating private audits exist.
